source_text: Οὕτω γὰρ θαυμαστὸν καὶ περισπούσαστόν ἐστι τὸ μαρτύριον, ὅτι αὐτὸς ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, τιμῶν αὐτὸ ἐμαρτύρησεν, »οὐχ ἁρπαγμὸν‘ ἡγησάμενος »τὸ εἶναι ἴσα θεῷ«, ἴνα καὶ τούτῳ τὸν ἄνθρωπον τῷ χαρίσματι εἰς ὅν κατέγβη στέφῃ.
thought_title: Christ honored martyrdom by his own witness
orientation: Methodius opens his treatise by praising martyrdom, saying that the Lord Jesus Christ himself honored it by bearing witness to it.
pass_a_gloss: Thus for wondrous and much-sought-after is the martyrdom, because himself the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, honoring it bore witness, "not a thing to be grasped" having considered "the being equal to God", in order that also with this the man with the gift into which he came down he might crown.

choices.why: Keeps the literal sense of eagerly pursued or sought after, matching the superlative praise of martyrdom without smoothing it into 'precious' or 'desirable'.
The verb is the cognate of μαρτύριον, so rendering it as 'bore witness' preserves the wordplay that Christ honored martyrdom by the act of witnessing.

choices.term: οὐχ ἁρπαγμὸν ἡγησάμενος τὸ εἶναι ἴσα θεῷ
choices.english: not considering being equal with God something to be grasped
choices.why: Follows the glossary for ἁρπαγμός and keeps the participle as a finite-relative clause in English, preserving the quoted wording of Philippians 2:6.
rejected: did not regard equality with God as something to be exploited
thought it not robbery to be equal with God

choices.term: ἴνα καὶ τούτῳ τὸν ἄνθρωπον τῷ χαρίσματι εἰς ὅν κατέγβη στέφῃ
choices.english: so that also with this gift he might crown the man into whom he descended
choices.why: Keeps the purpose clause, the dative of instrument 'with this gift', and the relative clause 'into whom he descended' in source order, preserving the literal force.
rejected: so that by this grace he might crown the man he came down to
in order that he might crown with this gift the man into whom he came down

bible_refs.note: οὐχ ἁρπαγμὸν ἡγησάμενος τὸ εἶναι ἴσα θεῷ

pass_b_english: For martyrdom is so wonderful and so much-sought-after that the Lord Jesus Christ himself, the Son of God, honored it by bearing witness to it, "not considering being equal with God something to be grasped" (Philippians 2:6), so that also with this gift he might crown the man into whom he descended.
